posts.seoTitle: Air Supply tour dates and prices | TourTicketCompare
posts.description: Air Supply listed prices by city from TicketNetwork, Vivid Seats and StubHub International, captured 2026-11-09, with venues and dates.
posts.summary: Where each ticket site listed its lowest Air Supply prices on 2026-11-09, city by city, and where to compare listings for your own date.
posts.author: TourTicketCompare

sections.content:
If price matters most, start with Hollywood, Rockford and Rancho Mirage: on 2026-11-09, StubHub International listed USD 63 for Hollywood, TicketNetwork's lowest listed price across its dates was USD 71 for Rockford, and Vivid Seats' lowest typical listing was USD 75 for Hollywood. Nothing can be said yet about movement, because the captured data carries no 30-day history for these dates.

Every figure below is one site's lowest listed price for that date when it was captured on 2026-11-09, in the currency the site listed. It is not a checkout total, and fees, delivery and the final price are set by the ticket site, so confirm them there before paying.

sections.title: Where each site lists its lowest prices

sections.title: What has moved
sections.content:
These are figures from a single capture day, and the data holds no 30-day record for any of these dates, so there is no movement to report. None of the listings was flagged as unusually low against the same site's other dates either.

A single day's figure is a starting point, not a promise that the same seat or price will still be there when you check.

sections.title: Compare listings for your own date
sections.content:
Once you have a city in mind, open the [Air Supply artist board](/artists/air-supply) and check every site listed for that exact date before you pay, since a figure for one city says nothing about another.

Before you commit, the guide on [how to read a ticket listing](/guides/how-to-read-a-ticket-listing) helps you check what a listed price actually includes. If you are unsure whether you are buying from the original seller or a resale site, [primary vs resale concert tickets](/guides/primary-vs-resale-concert-tickets) sets out the difference. For travelling fans, [ticket delivery and transfer timing](/guides/ticket-delivery-and-transfer-timing) covers when tickets usually reach you.

sections.content:
If price matters most, the western dates carry the lowest listed prices in the 2026-11-07 capture: for [Oakland Arena on 2026-12-07](https://www.ticketmaster.com/gracie-abrams-the-look-at-my-oakland-california-12-07-2026/event/1C0064BB9D932123), StubHub International listed USD 21, TicketNetwork USD 22 and Vivid Seats USD 25, with Inglewood, Seattle and Glendale not far off. Over the past 30 days almost every figure moved down, and Nashville on TicketNetwork is the one that went up.

Every figure below is that site's lowest listed price for that date when it was captured on 2026-11-07, in the currency shown. It is not a checkout total, and it is not a statement about what is on sale; confirm the full price on the ticket site before you pay.

sections.title: What moved over the last 30 days
sections.content:
Most of these figures are lower than they were a month earlier. Glendale fell on every site: StubHub International went from USD 47 to USD 25, TicketNetwork from USD 69 to USD 38 and Vivid Seats from USD 53 to USD 31. Chicago fell too, with TicketNetwork going from USD 122 to USD 76. Oakland, Inglewood and Seattle all dropped on every site, and Atlanta and Boston moved down too.

A few did not follow. TicketNetwork's Nashville figure rose from USD 62 to USD 71. Vivid Seats in Nashville stayed at USD 70, TicketNetwork in Charlotte stayed at USD 62, and Vivid Seats in Portland was about the same, USD 67 then USD 68. Austin has no figure from 30 days earlier, so there is nothing to compare there.

This is what already happened. It says nothing about where prices go next.

sections.title: Listings worth checking first
sections.content: Some of the lowest figures sit far below that site's other dates: all three Oakland listings (StubHub International USD 21, TicketNetwork USD 22, Vivid Seats USD 25), StubHub International USD 22 and Vivid Seats USD 27 in Inglewood, and StubHub International USD 23 in Seattle. Open the listing on the ticket site and check what it actually is before you plan around it. The guide on [how to read a ticket listing](/guides/how-to-read-a-ticket-listing) covers what to look at, and [ticket delivery and transfer timing](/guides/ticket-delivery-and-transfer-timing) explains when tickets usually reach you.

sections.title: Compare your own date
sections.content: Once you have a city in mind, pull up that exact date on the [Gracie Abrams artist board](/artists/gracie-abrams) and the [Gracie Abrams price guide](/artists/gracie-abrams/ticket-prices), then compare each site's listing for that show before paying. If you are weighing a resale listing against the original seller, [primary vs resale concert tickets](/guides/primary-vs-resale-concert-tickets) sets out the difference.

sections.title: What moved over the last 30 days
sections.content:
This is history, not a forecast. Prices can move either way from here.

Upward moves were common. Boston went from USD 116 to USD 133 on StubHub International, USD 152 to USD 194 on TicketNetwork and USD 131 to USD 153 on Vivid Seats. Chicago rose from USD 168 to USD 182 on StubHub International, USD 246 to USD 268 on TicketNetwork and USD 191 to USD 204 on Vivid Seats. Newark followed the same direction: USD 129 to USD 146 on StubHub International, USD 189 to USD 214 on TicketNetwork, USD 148 to USD 166 on Vivid Seats.

Vivid Seats also rose in Belmont Park (USD 133 to USD 141), Hamilton (USD 165 to USD 186) and Orlando (USD 127 to USD 130). Detroit was split: StubHub International rose from USD 102 to USD 119 and Vivid Seats from USD 117 to USD 136, while TicketNetwork stayed at USD 136.

A few listings went the other way. Cincinnati dropped from USD 93 to USD 82 on StubHub International and from USD 137 to USD 91 on TicketNetwork. Charlotte eased from USD 111 to USD 107 on StubHub International, with TicketNetwork unchanged at USD 144 and Vivid Seats up slightly, from USD 124 to USD 126. Philadelphia moved in both directions: TicketNetwork fell from USD 153 to USD 129, while StubHub International rose from USD 111 to USD 126 and Vivid Seats from USD 124 to USD 147. Quebec on TicketNetwork was about the same, USD 200 then USD 202.

sections.title: Two Orlando listings to check first
sections.content: The Orlando figures on StubHub International (USD 51, down from USD 113) and TicketNetwork (USD 54, down from USD 147) sit far below what those sites list for their other dates. They may be fine. Still, open the listing on the ticket site and check the section, quantity and full price before relying on either number. The guide on [how to read a ticket listing](/guides/how-to-read-a-ticket-listing) covers what to look for.

sections.title: Compare your own date
sections.content: Once you have a city in mind, compare listed prices for that exact date on the [Hans Zimmer artist board](/artists/hans-zimmer) and the [Hans Zimmer ticket price guide](/artists/hans-zimmer/ticket-prices). If you are weighing resale against the official seller, the guide to [primary vs resale concert tickets](/guides/primary-vs-resale-concert-tickets) sets out the difference, and [ticket delivery and transfer timing](/guides/ticket-delivery-and-transfer-timing) is a useful read before you pay.

Orlando moved the most in the other direction. StubHub International went from USD 20 to USD 62 and TicketNetwork from USD 30 to USD 87, while Vivid Seats went from USD 90 to USD 66.

Boston edged up on every site: StubHub International from USD 78 to USD 81, TicketNetwork from USD 91 to USD 94, Vivid Seats from USD 88 to USD 91. Vivid Seats in Brooklyn and Toronto and TicketNetwork in Chicago stayed about the same.

posts.title: Which US cities are cheapest for seeing a touring show?
posts.seoTitle: Cheapest US cities to see a tour | TourTicketCompare
posts.description: Across 100+ US tours, resale listings in Pittsburgh, Nashville and Miami sat below the tour's typical price; New York and San Francisco sat above it.
posts.summary: Across more than 100 US tours tracked in autumn 2026, the lowest listed resale price in Pittsburgh, Nashville and Miami was below the tour's typical price on both Vivid Seats and TicketNetwork in both September and October. New York and San Francisco were above it every time.
posts.author: TourTicketCompare

sections.content:
Where you see a tour can matter as much as when. TourTicketCompare keeps a daily record of the lowest listed resale price for the shows it tracks. For each US tour with five or more priced dates, it compared every city's price with the tour's typical show price, then looked at which cities came in cheaper or dearer across many tours.

Three cities came in below the tour's typical price on both sites and in both months checked: **Pittsburgh, Nashville and Miami**. Two came in above it every time: **New York and San Francisco**.

sections.title: The cities
sections.content:
October 2026, for US shows after that month. The figure is how far the city's price typically sat from the tour's typical show price. "Tours" is how many tours played that city. Each site is compared only with itself.

| City | Vivid Seats tours | Vivid Seats vs tour | TicketNetwork tours | TicketNetwork vs tour |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cleveland | 13 | −9.6% | 17 | −9.5% |
| Kansas City | 20 | −6.5% | 22 | −9.6% |
| Pittsburgh | 20 | −6.1% | 23 | −9.8% |
| Detroit | 27 | −5.6% | 32 | −10.5% |
| Miami | 13 | −6.8% | 16 | −5.5% |
| Nashville | 39 | −4.7% | 42 | −9.2% |
| Indianapolis | 17 | −5.0% | 18 | −3.0% |
| New York | 53 | +2.8% | 56 | +3.3% |
| Minneapolis | 17 | +2.2% | 25 | +5.9% |
| Portland | 26 | +8.6% | 31 | +11.4% |
| San Francisco | 36 | +2.8% | 41 | +14.7% |
| Salt Lake City | 16 | +18.3% | 16 | +25.1% |

In September 2026, with fewer tours, Pittsburgh, Nashville and Miami were again cheaper on both sites, and New York and San Francisco were again dearer. Cleveland, Kansas City and Salt Lake City had too few tours that month to check. Chicago, Los Angeles, Seattle, Atlanta and Las Vegas sat close to the tour's typical price.

The October readings cover 105 tours and 1,651 shows on Vivid Seats and 116 tours and 1,849 shows on TicketNetwork. No single tour made up more than about 3% of shows.

sections.title: What this does and doesn't say
sections.content:
- **It is the typical pattern, not every tour.** Even in the cheapest cities, some tours were dearer than elsewhere. Check the dates for the tour you want.
- **It is the lowest listed price, not every seat.** Venue size and layout differ by city, and a cheaper figure can mean more cheap seats were listed.
- **Nearby venues count with their metro.** For example, Inglewood counts as Los Angeles, and Brooklyn and East Rutherford count as New York.
- **It is resale, not face value,** and a listed price is not a checkout total. Fees, delivery and seat location differ between listings and between sites.
- **It compares listed prices as each site gave them.** TourTicketCompare has not confirmed how each site builds a listed price, and price-display rules can differ by state, so part of a city's gap could come from how prices are shown rather than what tickets cost.
- **It does not include travel.** A cheaper ticket in another city can cost more once you add the trip.

The method: for each show, TourTicketCompare took the middle daily lowest listed price across the month on one site. For each tour, it divided each city's price by the tour's middle show price, then took the middle of those figures across every tour that played the city. Cities needed 12 or more tours in October (10 in September). Prices below $5 or above $1,200 were left out as placeholders or outliers.

For a single tour, the [same tour, different city report](/blog/same-tour-different-city-ticket-prices) names the cheapest and dearest city for each artist. For the current listed price of any show, with the time it was checked, open the artist's page.

posts.title: How much do resale concert ticket prices move from day to day?
posts.seoTitle: How often do ticket prices change? | TourTicketCompare
posts.description: For about 1,200 US shows, the lowest resale listing jumped or fell by a fifth overnight at least once at about half of them.
posts.summary: Across about 1,200 US concerts tracked daily from September to early November 2026, the lowest listed resale price was unchanged on most days, but at 47% to 68% of shows (depending on the site) it moved by a fifth or more overnight at least once. At 18% to 28% of shows the highest daily low was at least double the lowest.
posts.author: TourTicketCompare

sections.content: Most days, the cheapest resale ticket for a concert costs the same as it did the day before. But when it moves, it can move a lot. TourTicketCompare keeps a daily record of the lowest listed price on Vivid Seats, TicketNetwork and StubHub International for the shows it tracks. For US shows with at least 30 days of prices between 1 September and 2 November 2026, the lowest listing was unchanged from one day to the next about two times in three. Yet at about half of shows it jumped or fell by 20% or more overnight at least once.

sections.title: Site by site
sections.content:
Each row covers one site's own listings. "Unchanged" means within half a percent of the day before.

| Site | Shows | Artists | Days unchanged | Shows with a 20%+ overnight move | Shows where the high was 2× the low |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vivid Seats | 1,195 | 79 | 66% | 560 (47%) | 217 (18%) |
| TicketNetwork | 1,233 | 82 | 71% | 844 (68%) | 347 (28%) |
| StubHub International | 533 | 58 | 63% | 315 (59%) | 130 (24%) |

No single artist made up more than about 10% of any site's shows. Sites list different seats with different fees, so this does not compare one site with another.

sections.title: What it looks like
sections.content:
Vivid Seats, lowest listed price at the last check of the day (days in UTC):

- **Gracie Abrams, Inglewood, 19 December 2026.** About $90 on 1 September 2026, down to $32 on 23 October.
- **Gracie Abrams, Oakland, 6 December 2026.** About $99 on 2 September 2026, down to $33 on 31 October.

Those two fell, but big moves went both ways. A price that drops overnight can come back the next day.

sections.title: The second night of a run is not cheaper
sections.content: Some fans assume the extra date added to a sold-out run is the cheap one. TourTicketCompare compared back-to-back nights by the same artist at the same venue, using each night's typical lowest listing in October 2026. On Vivid Seats, the second night was cheaper in 85 of 223 pairs and dearer in 102. On TicketNetwork it was cheaper in 96 of 210 and dearer in 80, and on StubHub International cheaper in 77 of 193 and dearer in 94. There was no consistent pattern either way.

sections.title: What this does and doesn't say
sections.content:
- **It is the lowest listed price, not every seat.** A big move can be one cheap listing appearing or selling, not every ticket changing price.
- **It is daily, not live.** Prices can change several times a day. This records the last check of each day.
- **It is not a forecast.** It shows how often prices moved, not which way the next move will go.
- **It is US shows only,** and covers September to early November 2026.
- **A listed price is not a checkout total.** Fees, delivery and seat location differ between listings and between sites.

Prices below $5 or above $1,200 were left out as placeholders or outliers.

Because prices can change overnight, check the time next to any price before you buy. For the current listed price of any show, open the artist's page. The [guide to why ticket prices change](/guides/why-ticket-prices-change) explains what moves them.

posts.title: Which US tours got cheaper on resale this month? November 2026
posts.seoTitle: Tours that got cheaper: Nov 2026 | TourTicketCompare
posts.description: Across 1,072 upcoming US concert dates, resale prices fell twice as often as they rose in the month to 5 November 2026. The tours that moved most.
posts.summary: TourTicketCompare compared the lowest listed resale price for 1,072 upcoming US concert dates in early October and early November 2026, each site against itself. Falls outnumbered rises 1,201 to 621. Greta Van Fleet and Gracie Abrams dates fell most; John Summit and Don Omar dates rose.
posts.author: TourTicketCompare

sections.content: TourTicketCompare keeps a daily record of the lowest listed resale price on Vivid Seats, TicketNetwork and StubHub International for the concerts it tracks. For this report it took every upcoming US date that had a price on the same site in both 5 to 7 October and 3 to 5 November 2026, and compared each one with itself a month earlier. That gave 2,344 comparisons across 1,072 dates by 71 artists. The lowest listed price was lower at 1,201 of them, higher at 621, and within 2% at the rest. The typical move was a fall of about 2%.

sections.title: Site by site
sections.content:
Each row compares one site only with its own listings a month earlier. Sites list different seats with different fees, so this does not say which site is lower for any show.

| Site | Dates | Artists | Lower | Higher | Within 2% | Typical move |

| Vivid Seats | 965 | 68 | 475 | 251 | 239 | -1.7% |
| TicketNetwork | 981 | 71 | 526 | 233 | 222 | -3.1% |
| StubHub International | 398 | 49 | 200 | 137 | 61 | -2.3% |

Falls outnumbered rises on every site.

These are the tours with 8 or more US dates in the comparison where the typical date moved by 5% or more, at least two sites had 5 or more of the tour's dates, and every such site moved the same way. "Typical move" is the median change across all of the tour's site-and-date comparisons.

| Artist | Dates | Lower | Higher | Typical move |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| [Sombr](/artists/sombr) | 8 | 16 | 4 | -11% |
| [Harry Styles](/artists/harry-styles) | 18 | 32 | 15 | -9% |
| [Pentatonix](/artists/pentatonix) | 23 | 33 | 13 | -8% |
| [The Red Clay Strays](/artists/the-red-clay-strays) | 24 | 40 | 2 | -8% |
| [Tyla](/artists/tyla) | 18 | 29 | 16 | -6% |
| [Niall Horan](/artists/niall-horan) | 21 | 32 | 10 | -6% |
| [Missio](/artists/missio) | 17 | 17 | 3 | -5% |

"Lower" and "Higher" count site-and-date comparisons, so a date listed on three sites counts up to three times.

The biggest move was Greta Van Fleet's 2027 tour. Every one of its 69 comparisons was lower. On Vivid Seats, the median lowest listed price across its 35 dates was $123 in early October and $65 in early November, and on TicketNetwork across 34 dates $140 and $86 respectively (USD, listed prices, medians of 5 to 7 October and 3 to 5 November 2026).

Gracie Abrams dates, which run from December 2026 to March 2027, were lower at 86 of 99 comparisons. On Vivid Seats the median across 33 dates was $63 in early October and $46 in early November.

sections.title: The tours that got dearer
sections.content:
| Artist | Dates | Lower | Higher | Typical move |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [John Summit](/artists/john-summit) | 12 | 3 | 28 | +31% |

John Summit's dates, from mid-November to mid-December 2026, rose on all three sites. On Vivid Seats the median across 11 dates was $61 in early October and $75 in early November.

sections.title: Big tours that barely moved
sections.content: Some of the most-searched tours had no clear direction over the month. Olivia Rodrigo's 35 US dates had a typical move of 0% across 105 comparisons. Metallica's 18 dates moved in different directions on different sites. Hans Zimmer's 26 dates rose on every site, but the typical move (+4.6%) was just under this report's 5% bar.

sections.title: What this does and doesn't say
sections.content:
- **It is a record of one month, not a forecast.** A tour that fell this month can rise next month. Every date was a month closer to the show at the second reading, which is part of what this measures.
- **It is the lowest listed price, not every seat.** A big move can be one cheap listing appearing or selling.
- **It is US dates only,** in US dollars, and only dates still more than a week away on 6 November 2026.
- **A listed price is not a checkout total.** Fees, delivery and seat location differ between listings and between sites.

Each reading is the median of the last daily check on each of three days. Dates without a price on at least two of the three days at both ends were left out (80 comparisons), and so were 5 comparisons with a price of $1,000 or more, which are treated as placeholders. TourTicketCompare will repeat this comparison each month.

posts.title: Should you rush to buy resale tickets for a new tour?
posts.seoTitle: Should you rush to buy resale tickets? | TourTicketCompare
posts.description: For 1,608 US shows on new tours, the lowest resale listing two weeks after TourTicketCompare first recorded it was lower at about half and higher at a quarter.
posts.summary: Across 1,608 US concerts on newly listed tours in autumn 2026, the lowest listed resale price two weeks after TourTicketCompare first recorded it was lower at 49% of shows and higher at 24%. Prices fell about twice as often as they rose, but there was no fall at half the shows.
posts.author: TourTicketCompare

sections.content:
Rushing to buy resale tickets for a new tour rarely paid off. TourTicketCompare keeps a daily record of the lowest listed price on Vivid Seats, TicketNetwork and StubHub International for the shows it tracks. For 1,608 US concerts by 100 artists whose first recorded price fell between 9 August and 19 October 2026, the lowest listed price two weeks later was lower than on that first day at 788 of them (49%). It was higher at 390 (24%) and about the same at 430. The typical change was a fall of 1.8%, about $1.40.

So prices fell about twice as often as they rose. That is a record of what happened on these tours, not a forecast, and at a quarter of the shows the price went up.

sections.title: Site by site
sections.content:
Each row compares one site with itself, for the same show, on the first day TourTicketCompare recorded a price and 14 days later. "About the same" means within 2% either way.

| Site | Shows | Lower | Higher | About the same |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vivid Seats | 1,081 | 518 | 326 | 237 |
| TicketNetwork | 1,215 | 616 | 265 | 334 |
| StubHub International | 283 | 117 | 88 | 78 |

On every site, falls outnumbered rises. Sites list different seats with different fees, so this does not compare one site with another.

sections.title: How big the moves were
sections.content: Most changes were small. At 13% of shows (208) the lowest listing fell by a quarter or more in the first fortnight, and at 5% (74) it rose by a quarter or more. A big drop was more common than a big rise, but neither was the norm. After one week the picture was similar: lower at 696 shows, higher at 330.

sections.title: Three shows, day by day
sections.content:
Each figure is the lowest listed price on that site at its last check of the day (days in UTC).

- **Harry Styles, Atlanta, 21 May 2027.** Vivid Seats: $586 on 11 September 2026, the first day it was recorded, then $211 a week later and $101 after two weeks.
- **Fontaines D.C., Atlanta, 8 October 2027.** TicketNetwork: $184 on 4 October 2026, $46 a week later and $42.55 after two weeks.
- **Carly Rae Jepsen, Chicago, 21 May 2027.** The other way: TicketNetwork was $163.30 on 4 October 2026, then $227.70 a week later and $326.60 after two weeks.

sections.title: What this does and doesn't say
sections.content:
- **The first day is when TourTicketCompare first recorded a price, not the official on-sale date.** A show can enter the records on its on-sale day or days or weeks later, once its links are verified, so this describes the first fortnight of tracking, not the first fortnight of sales.
- **It is the lowest listed price, not every seat.** A lower starting price can mean a cheaper listing appeared, not that every ticket got cheaper.
- **It is not a rule.** About half the shows had no fall, and a quarter got dearer. It covers tours listed in summer and autumn 2026 only.
- **It is US shows only.** TourTicketCompare tracks too few shows elsewhere to say anything yet.
- **It says nothing about face value.** Official tickets at face value are a different market, and when they sell out, resale may be the only option.
- **A listed price is not a checkout total.** Fees, delivery and seat location differ between listings and between sites. Check the full total on the ticket site before you pay.

To see which tours' prices have fallen or risen lately, with sample sizes, use [Is it worth waiting?](/is-it-worth-waiting). For the current listed price of any show, with the time it was checked, open the artist's page. For the other end of the buying window, see [what happened to prices in the final week before a show](/blog/do-concert-ticket-prices-drop-in-the-last-week). The [guide to when to buy concert tickets](/guides/when-is-the-best-time-to-buy-concert-tickets) covers the trade-offs beyond price: seat choice, group seating and delivery time.

posts.title: Beyoncé 2027 tour: what is known so far
posts.seoTitle: Beyoncé 2027 tour: what is known so far | TourTicketCompare
posts.description: No Beyoncé tour has been announced. What has been reported about a 2027 run, what is only speculation, and how to avoid buying for a date that does not exist.
posts.summary: As of 2 November 2026 Beyoncé has not announced a tour. A 2027 run has been predicted and rumoured, but none of it is confirmed. Here is what is reported, what is not, and what to do before an announcement.
posts.author: TourTicketCompare

sections.content:
**No Beyoncé tour has been announced.** As of 2 November 2026 there are no confirmed dates, cities or on-sale times, and no official ticket link exists to buy from. The Beyoncé artist page here lists no shows for that reason.

Everything below about 2027 is prediction or rumour. It is separated into what is reported and what is only guessed, so you can judge how much weight to give each part.

sections.title: What has been reported
sections.content:
- **A prediction, not an announcement.** A 19 February 2026 piece in Dazed is built on patterns rather than inside information. It expects an album in 2026 and, going by her past gaps, a tour in 2027: "If our calculations are correct, Bey will be touring Act III in 2027." The piece itself says nothing about Act III or a tour is confirmed.
- **A rumour with a shaky source.** Entertainment site Mediamass says Beyoncé is rumoured to be planning a worldwide tour at the end of 2027. The same page says a representative had no information about future plans when contacted.
- **Fan-account claims.** Posts on social media have claimed that her team is already booking stadiums, including in the UK. These name no source that can be checked, so treat them as unconfirmed.

sections.title: What has not been confirmed
sections.content: No dates, no cities, no venues, no ticket prices, no presale or general on-sale. Any page that gives you those for a 2027 Beyoncé tour is guessing. Some third-party sites already show 2027 "tour dates" or "presale soon" notices, and nothing in the sources above backs them up.

sections.title: What happened last time
sections.content: Her previous run, the Cowboy Carter Tour, was announced on Sunday 2 February 2025 through two posts on Instagram, according to Revolt. The announcement came from her directly, not from a rumour that turned into a listing. That is the pattern to wait for again: an announcement from Beyoncé herself, then ticket links from the official sellers.

sections.title: What to do before an announcement
sections.content:
1. **Do not pay for anything now.** Until a tour is announced there is no real date, seat or ticket to buy. A listing for a show that has not been announced is a bet on the show, not a ticket.
2. **Sign up for date alerts** on the [Beyoncé artist page](/artists/beyonce) to get an email when dates are published.
3. **Check where a link goes** once dates exist. Dates and venues should match the official announcement before you rely on a link.
4. **Know the difference between primary and resale** before the first sale. [Primary vs resale concert tickets](/guides/primary-vs-resale-concert-tickets) explains who you are buying from, and [how to read a ticket listing](/guides/how-to-read-a-ticket-listing) covers what to check on a listing. [Ticket delivery and transfer timing](/guides/ticket-delivery-and-transfer-timing) explains why a resale ticket may not arrive straight away.

This page will be updated when a tour is announced or the reporting changes.

sections.title: How to read this

- **"Typical lowest price"** is the median, the middle value, of the lowest listed prices across a tour's US dates. "Middle half of dates" runs from the 25th to the 75th percentile, so it shows how much the dates differ within one tour.
- **Each date's figure** is the lowest listed price among the resale sites TourTicketCompare checks (Vivid Seats, TicketNetwork and StubHub International). A price far below every other site's price for the same show is treated as a feed error and left out, as is anything under $10.
- **Included:** United States dates in US dollars, at least a week away, from the newest reading in the last three days. Final-week readings are left out because some feeds show placeholder prices then. 124 tours and 2053 dates are counted, and no tour is more than 3% of them.
- **A listed price is not a checkout total.** Fees and delivery are added at the ticket site, and the cheapest seats differ between a stadium and a theatre, so a bigger venue can look cheaper or dearer for reasons that have nothing to do with the artist.
- **This is a snapshot, not a forecast.** It says what listings cost when they were checked, not what they will cost later.

posts.title: Do resale concert ticket prices drop in the last week?
posts.seoTitle: Do ticket prices drop in the last week? | TourTicketCompare
posts.description: At 6 in 10 of 421 US concerts, the lowest resale listing fell in the final week. On show day itself, prices fell at half and rose at nearly 4 in 10.
posts.summary: Across 421 US concerts between late July and October 2026, the lowest listed resale price was lower the day before the show than a week earlier at about 6 in 10 of them. Waiting until show day itself was closer to a coin flip.
posts.author: TourTicketCompare

sections.content:
Waiting until the final week paid off more often than not. TourTicketCompare keeps a daily record of the lowest listed price on Vivid Seats, TicketNetwork and StubHub International for the shows it tracks. For 421 US concerts by 68 artists, held between 28 July and 29 October 2026, the lowest listed price the day before the show was lower than seven days before at 250 of them (59%). It was higher at 133 (32%) and about the same at 38. The typical change was a fall of 6.7%, about $6.

That is a record of what happened at these shows, not a forecast. At almost a third of them, the price went the other way.

sections.title: Site by site
sections.content:
Each row compares one site with itself, for the same show, seven days out and the day before. "About the same" means within 2% either way.

| Site | Shows | Lower | Higher | About the same |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vivid Seats | 367 | 218 | 114 | 35 |
| TicketNetwork | 365 | 218 | 133 | 14 |
| StubHub International | 259 | 155 | 69 | 35 |

The three sites point the same way: on each, the lowest listing fell before about 6 in 10 shows. Sites list different seats with different fees, so this does not compare one site with another.

sections.title: How big the moves were
sections.content: Most changes were modest. At 23% of shows the lowest listing fell by a quarter or more in the final week, and at 14% it rose by a quarter or more. A big drop was more common than a big rise, but neither was the norm.

sections.title: Show day itself is a gamble
sections.content:
From the day before the show to the day of it, the picture is much less clear. For 521 US shows by 89 artists, the lowest listed price on show day was lower at 258 (50%), higher at 198 (38%) and about the same at 65. The typical change was a fall of 1.6%, about $1.50.

| Site | Shows | Lower | Higher | About the same |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vivid Seats | 461 | 216 | 167 | 78 |
| TicketNetwork | 446 | 219 | 188 | 39 |
| StubHub International | 300 | 153 | 94 | 53 |

So holding out for the day itself was close to a coin flip, and it leaves little time to sort out a transfer or a sign-in problem before the doors open.

sections.title: Three shows, day by day
sections.content:
Each figure is the lowest listed price on that site at its last check of the day (days in UTC).

- **Katseye, Boston, 28 October.** Vivid Seats: $220 on 22 October, $123 on 27 October, $58 on show day. StubHub International: $211.57, $122.50, then $94.66.
- **Phoebe Bridgers, San Francisco, 27 October.** Vivid Seats: $81 on 20 October, $76 on 26 October, $28 on show day. StubHub International: $73.09, $59.73, then $26.
- **Ariana Grande, Montreal, 31 July** (a Canadian show, so not in the US counts above). Vivid Seats: $524.91 on 24 July, $148.83 on 30 July, then back up to $207.09 on show day. TicketNetwork: $456.50, $146.30, then $227.70.

sections.title: What this does and doesn't say
sections.content:
- **It is the lowest listed price, not every seat.** A lower starting price can mean a cheaper listing appeared further back, not that every ticket got cheaper.
- **It is not a rule.** Prices rose in the final week at about a third of these shows, and the post covers summer and autumn 2026 only.
- **It is US shows only.** TourTicketCompare tracks too few shows elsewhere to say anything yet.
- **Earlier than a week out, there is no clear pattern.** Over the month before a show, the direction depended mostly on the artist, so this post makes no claim about buying a month ahead.
- **A listed price is not a checkout total.** Fees, delivery and seat location differ between listings and between sites. Check the full total on the ticket site before you pay.

For the current listed price of any show, with the time it was checked, open the artist's page. The [guide to when to buy concert tickets](/guides/when-is-the-best-time-to-buy-concert-tickets) covers the trade-offs beyond price: seat choice, group seating and delivery time.

posts.title: Harry Styles tour: dates, cities and how to choose
posts.seoTitle: Harry Styles tour dates by city | TourTicketCompare
posts.description: Harry Styles dates in Australia, North America and Europe, with the weekday for each city and a checklist for comparing listings for one exact show.
posts.summary: Choose a Harry Styles city by region and weekday, then compare listings for that exact date on the artist board and price guide before paying.
posts.author: TourTicketCompare

sections.content:
Start with the region you can realistically reach, then let the weekday decide between the cities in it. Once you have a date, compare listings for that exact show, matched on date, venue and city, before you pay anything.

The dates below come from Ticketmaster's own event pages. Each one was re-checked against Ticketmaster's official listing on 2026-10-26 for the artist, local date, venue and city. Confirm everything on the official event page before buying, because a listing check is not a guarantee about the show or about tickets.

sections.title: The cities by region
sections.content:
The table shows one date per city. The [Harry Styles artist board](/artists/harry-styles) has every other tracked date.

sections.title: What actually differs between them
sections.content:
The useful differences here are the region, the weekday and the season you would be travelling in. Nothing in the listings suggests a reason to rank one city's show above another's, so do not go looking for one.

**Weekday.** Most of the dates in the table fall on a Friday. If you are travelling, that usually means leaving after work or taking the Friday off, then having the weekend to get home. The [Sydney Olympic Park](https://www.ticketmaster.com.au/harry-styles-together-together-sydney-olympic-park-12-12-2026/event/250064346C5043CE) date is a Saturday, which leaves Sunday free for the trip back. [Dublin](https://www.ticketmaster.ie/harry-styles-together-together-dublin-18-08-2027/event/18006529A226B959) and [London](https://www.ticketmaster.co.uk/harry-styles-together-together-london-25-08-2027/event/2300650EC5AF20F8) are both Wednesdays. A midweek stadium show is easy if you live nearby and harder if you need a hotel and time off on either side.

**Region and timing.** The Australian stops come before the North American ones, and the European stops come after. If one region is a long way from you, the gap before its date gives you more room to plan travel and leave.

**Which country site lists it.** Ticketmaster lists each city on its own country site: .com.au for the Australian stops, .ca for Toronto, .ie for Dublin, .co.uk for London and .com for the US cities.

sections.title: Make sure two listings are the same show
sections.content:
Resale listings and screenshots do not always describe a show the way Ticketmaster does. Before comparing two prices, check that both match on all of these:

- **Date in venue-local time.** The dates above are local to each venue. A site showing times in your own zone can make a date look different.
- **Venue name.** Marvel Stadium, Accor Stadium, Rose Bowl and so on, not just the city.
- **City as listed.** Ticketmaster lists the Australian venues under Docklands and Sydney Olympic Park. Another site may use a broader place name, so match the venue as well.
- **Ticket type and quantity.** Same section type, same number of tickets.

The [guide to reading a ticket listing](/guides/how-to-read-a-ticket-listing) covers seat details and restrictions. If you are weighing a primary ticket against a resale one, see [primary vs resale concert tickets](/guides/primary-vs-resale-concert-tickets). For a show you are flying to, [ticket delivery and transfer timing](/guides/ticket-delivery-and-transfer-timing) explains when tickets tend to land in your account.

sections.title: Compare listed prices for your date
sections.content: Once you have settled on a city and date, open the [Harry Styles ticket price guide](/artists/harry-styles/ticket-prices), then the [artist board](/artists/harry-styles) for the ticket sites. Open the listing for your exact date and confirm the date, seat details, fees and final total on the ticket site before paying. Pick the listing that suits you best.

posts.title: Metallica tour: dates, cities and how to choose
posts.seoTitle: Metallica tour dates: pick a city | TourTicketCompare
posts.description: The first listed Metallica date in each city, grouped by region and weekday, with a checklist for comparing listings for your exact date.
posts.summary: Pick the Metallica city and date that fits your week and travel, then compare listings for that exact date. Saturday dates suit weekend trips. Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday dates mean planning around work.
posts.author: TourTicketCompare

sections.content:
Start by choosing the city and weekday that fit your life, then compare listings only for that exact date. A Saturday show close to home is the easiest trip to plan. A midweek date in another city can still make sense, but it means booking time off and travel around the show.

The dates below come from Ticketmaster's event listings. The table shows one date per city, so check the [Metallica page](/artists/metallica) for every other date before deciding.

sections.title: Weekday matters more than it looks
sections.content:
The Saturday dates are Vancouver, San Antonio, Kansas City, Indianapolis and Salt Lake City. If you are travelling, a Saturday show lets you arrive Friday or Saturday morning and head home Sunday without losing a workday.

El Paso, Orchard Park and Cleveland fall on Tuesdays, and Fayetteville on a Wednesday. Those suit people who live nearby, or anyone happy to take a day or two off. Las Vegas and San Diego are Thursdays.

If you live between regions, line up the dates. Kansas City on a Saturday and Fayetteville on the Wednesday before it are close together in the calendar. So are Indianapolis and Orchard Park. The table gives you the dates. How far you will drive or fly is yours to work out.

sections.title: Las Vegas comes first
sections.content: The [Las Vegas date at Sphere](https://www.ticketmaster.com/metallica-life-burns-faster-las-vegas-nevada-01-28-2027/event/170064619015BB05) comes months before the other cities in this table. Treat it as its own decision, not as a swap for a later date. The [Metallica page](/artists/metallica) has every tracked Las Vegas date.

sections.title: Vancouver is on Ticketmaster's Canadian site
sections.content: The [Vancouver listing](https://www.ticketmaster.ca/metallica-m72-world-tour-vancouver-british-columbia-05-08-2027/event/1100652ED2CADD90) is on ticketmaster.ca, while the others are on ticketmaster.com. When you compare a Vancouver listing with one from a US city, check which currency each site shows at checkout before deciding one costs more than the other.

sections.title: What a checked link means
sections.content: TourTicketCompare keeps resale links that were matched to the exact event, and the [Metallica page](/artists/metallica) shows them for each date. A matched link does not tell you what is listed there right now, what it costs or whether the seats suit you. Open the ticket site to find out.

sections.title: Before you pay
sections.content:
Every listing shares the same artist name. What tells them apart is the city, venue and date, so check them against each other.

- **The date and city.** Confirm both on the listing and again on the order summary. A mistake here is easy to make and hard to undo.
- **The seat.** Section, row, whether the seats are together, and any restriction notes. The [guide to reading a ticket listing](/guides/how-to-read-a-ticket-listing) covers each label.
- **Who is selling.** The official Ticketmaster page and a resale site are different kinds of seller. The [primary versus resale guide](/guides/primary-vs-resale-concert-tickets) explains what changes.
- **When it arrives.** Resale tickets are often transferred close to the show. The [delivery and transfer guide](/guides/ticket-delivery-and-transfer-timing) explains the usual timing.
- **The total.** Compare the final checkout total for the same seats and quantity, not the first figure shown.

sections.title: Compare your date
sections.content: Once you have a city in mind, open the [Metallica ticket price guide](/artists/metallica/ticket-prices). It shows listed resale prices by date, with each ticket site's name and the time it was checked. These are each site's listed prices at the time they were checked, not face value or final totals. The [Metallica page](/artists/metallica) has the ticket buttons for each tracked date, so you can compare the sites for your show and choose the listing that suits you.

posts.title: Choosing a Metallica night at Sphere
posts.seoTitle: Choosing a Metallica Sphere night | TourTicketCompare
posts.description: Metallica's Sphere residency runs in Thursday and Saturday pairs with two different sets. Which nights are left, and what to check before buying.
posts.summary: Metallica's Life Burns Faster residency at Sphere plays in Thursday and Saturday pairs, and the band bills each pair as a No Repeat Weekend with two different sets. That makes the night you pick, and whether a listing covers one night or two, worth more attention than usual.
posts.author: TourTicketCompare

sections.content: Metallica's Life Burns Faster residency at Sphere in Las Vegas plays on Thursdays and Saturdays, and each Thursday and Saturday pair is billed as a No Repeat Weekend: two shows with two different sets, the format the band used on the M72 World Tour. When the dates were extended, the fan club sale offered both single-night tickets and two-night No Repeat Weekend tickets. So a Metallica Sphere listing can differ in a way most listings don't: it may be for one night or for two.

sections.title: Compare the Las Vegas nights
sections.content: The [Metallica Las Vegas date comparison](/artists/metallica/ticket-prices#priceGuideCity-las-vegas-united-states) lists each Sphere night as its own row, with the ticket sites that have a checked link for that night. Where a price appears, it is one site's listed price for that one night, with the time it was checked. It isn't the face value or the final total, and it is never a price for a weekend pair. The [Metallica page](/artists/metallica) has the same nights with their ticket buttons, alongside the band's 2027 stadium dates.

sections.title: Remaining dates as of 28 October 2026
sections.content:
These dates remain on the [residency schedule published by Metallica](https://www.metallica.com/news/2026-02-25-life-burns-faster-at-sphere-in-las-vegas.html) as of 28 October 2026. Check the exact event listing for its current start time before booking travel.

| Weekend | Thursday | Saturday |
|---|---|---|
| October | 29 Oct (has passed) | 31 Oct (has passed) |
| November | 5 Nov | 7 Nov |
| January 2027 | 28 Jan | 30 Jan |
| February | 4 Feb | 6 Feb |
| February | 18 Feb | 20 Feb |
| February | 25 Feb | 27 Feb |
| March | 4 Mar | 6 Mar |
| March | 11 Mar | 13 Mar |

After 7 November there is a gap of almost three months before the residency returns on 28 January.

sections.title: Thursday, Saturday or both
sections.content:
The two nights of a weekend are not interchangeable. No listing can promise which songs a night will include, only that the two nights of a pair are billed as different sets. If seeing a broad slice of the catalogue matters to you, the pair is the way to get it. If one night is enough, either works, and the choice comes down to the date, the seat and the total.

Thursday and Saturday nights can also price differently on resale, because demand for each date is separate. Compare the two nights of the weekend you want before settling, rather than assuming they cost the same.

sections.title: What to check on the listing
sections.content:
- **One night or two.** A listing should say whether it covers a single night or both nights of a weekend. Confirm the admission covered in the ticket details; do not infer it from a single displayed date. The [band’s FAQ](https://www.metallica.com/help/2026-02-25-sphere-faqs.html) distinguishes single-night and two-night tickets, and says a two-night ticket transfers as a unit.
- **The date.** Every listing has the same artist, venue and show name. The date is the only thing that tells them apart, so check it on the listing and on the order summary.
- **The seat.** Where the listing places you matters as much as the night. The [guide to reading a ticket listing](/guides/how-to-read-a-ticket-listing) covers section, row and restriction notes.
- **Delivery.** Resale tickets for a residency night are often transferred close to the date. The [delivery and transfer guide](/guides/ticket-delivery-and-transfer-timing) explains what to expect.

posts.title: Eagles at Sphere, January 2027: presale and on-sale times
posts.seoTitle: Eagles Sphere 2027 presale times | TourTicketCompare
posts.description: Eagles added 8 and 9 January 2027 at Sphere. Presales open 28 and 29 October, general sale 30 October at 10:00 PT. What to check before buying.
posts.summary: Two more Eagles nights at Sphere in Las Vegas, Friday 8 and Saturday 9 January 2027, go on general sale on Friday 30 October at 10:00 Pacific time, after two days of presales. The other residency nights are already on sale, which shapes what you see on resale sites this week.
posts.author: TourTicketCompare

sections.content: Eagles have added two more nights to their Sphere residency in Las Vegas: Friday 8 January 2027 and Saturday 9 January 2027. Ticketmaster lists both with a public on-sale of Friday 30 October 2026 at 10:00 Pacific time, after presales on the two days before. The announcement, as reported on 21 October, puts the residency at 74 performances in total.

sections.title: The sale times for the two new nights
sections.content:
These are the windows Ticketmaster lists for both new dates. All times are Pacific, the venue's own time zone.

| Sale | Opens | Closes |
|---|---|---|
| Seated presale | Wed 28 Oct, 10:00 (opened) | Fri 30 Oct, 09:59 |
| On The List VIP package presale | Wed 28 Oct, 10:00 (opened) | Thu 29 Oct, 22:00 (closed) |
| Live Nation presale | Thu 29 Oct, 10:00 | Fri 30 Oct, 09:59 |
| Ticketmaster presale | Thu 29 Oct, 10:00 | Fri 30 Oct, 09:59 |
| Venue presale | Thu 29 Oct, 10:00 | Fri 30 Oct, 09:59 |
| General public on-sale | Fri 30 Oct, 10:00 | |

Ticketmaster lists both the Friday and Saturday shows at 8:30 PM, Las Vegas time (checked 28 October 2026). Presale names come from Ticketmaster's event listings. TourTicketCompare does not hold or publish presale codes, and how to qualify for each presale is set by whoever runs it. The [Eagles page](/artists/eagles) links the presale times for each date, and drops them once they close.

For UK readers, 10:00 Pacific on 28, 29 and 30 October is 17:00 in London. The clocks change in the UK on 25 October and in the US on 1 November, so the gap that week is seven hours, not the usual eight.

sections.title: The other nights are already on sale
sections.content:
The new January nights are not the only way in. Ticketmaster already lists twelve other Eagles nights at Sphere as on sale: 13 and 14 November, 27 and 28 November, 4 and 5 December, 11 and 12 December 2026, then 15, 16, 22 and 23 January 2027. Those nights have resale listings now, so a search for "Eagles Sphere tickets" this week mixes the new dates with dates that have been on sale for months.

On a residency, the venue and the show name are the same on every listing. The date is the only field that tells two listings apart, so check it on the listing and again on the order summary before you pay. The [guide to reading a ticket listing](/guides/how-to-read-a-ticket-listing) covers the other fields worth checking, and the [Eagles page](/artists/eagles) lists every tracked night with its own ticket buttons.

sections.title: Before and after 30 October
sections.content:
Before the general sale, the two new nights show their on-sale time on the Eagles page and no Ticketmaster button. That does not mean presales are closed: check the Ticketmaster event listing for the current window and eligibility. Resale sites sometimes list seats for a date before its public on-sale. A listing like that is a seller's promise to deliver seats they expect to get, which is worth knowing before paying for one. The [primary vs resale guide](/guides/primary-vs-resale-concert-tickets) explains the difference.

After the general sale opens, the Eagles page adds the ticket sites with a checked link for each new night. Where a price appears next to a button, it is that site's listed price for that one night when it was last checked, with the time shown. It isn't the face value or the final total. Compare the seat, the fees and the delivery terms on the ticket site itself, and use the [on-sale checklist](/guides/how-to-prepare-for-a-ticket-onsale) if you plan to buy in the presale.

posts.seoTitle: Zach Bryan 2027 tour tickets | TourTicketCompare
posts.description: Zach Bryan's 2027 stadium dates went on general sale on 23 October. Which dates are listed, who opens each leg, and what to check on resale.
posts.summary: Zach Bryan's 2027 stadium tour went on general sale on Friday 23 October, at 10:00 in each venue's time zone, after two days of presales. Once the first sale is over, most buyers are choosing between a returned primary seat and a resale listing, and the details that matter change.
posts.author: TourTicketCompare

sections.content: Zach Bryan's 2027 stadium tour went on general sale on Friday 23 October 2026, at 10:00 local time for each venue, after artist and local presales on 21 and 22 October. The tour, as announced, runs from late April to August across North America, then to Australia in December. For most people still looking now, the question is no longer how to get through the queue. It is how to compare what is left.

sections.content: The [Zach Bryan page](/artists/zach-bryan) lists each checked date with its own ticket sites, and links the Zach Bryan price guide for a date-by-date view. Where a price appears, it is one site's listed price for that one date, with the time it was checked. It isn't the face value or a final checkout total.

sections.title: What to check on a stadium resale listing
sections.content:
A stadium listing has more ways to differ than an arena one. Three are worth checking every time.

- **Floor or seats.** A floor ticket may be standing general admission, and the listing should say so. The [floor or seats guide](/blog/floor-or-seats-at-a-stadium-concert) covers the trade-off.
- **Ticket type.** Ticketmaster lists a separate General Admission Early Entry sale for the Seattle date. A listing for that date should say whether early entry is included, and if it doesn't, assume it isn't.
- **Delivery date.** Resale sellers often can't transfer stadium tickets until close to the show. The [delivery and transfer guide](/guides/ticket-delivery-and-transfer-timing) explains what a late delivery date means and when to worry.

The [guide to reading a ticket listing](/guides/how-to-read-a-ticket-listing) goes through the rest. Whatever you buy, check the date and city on the order summary before paying. With two nights each at MetLife, BC Place and Commonwealth Stadium, the date is the field that separates one listing from another.

sections.title: What this does and doesn't say
sections.content:
- **These are listed prices.** Prices are each ticket site's listed price when it was last checked, at the time shown. They change often and aren't your final total. Some prices may already include fees. You'll see the full price, with taxes and delivery, on the ticket site before you pay.
- **A city gap is not a forecast.** A city that's high today can drop, and a low one can rise. Nothing here says when to buy.
- **Only the tours TourTicketCompare tracks.** Cities outside the tour's main country, and cities whose next date had no recent listed price on that site, are left out.

For every date and every site, with the current price, open the artist's page.

The [Warner Records announcement](https://press.warnerrecords.com/sites/g/files/g2000014901/files/2025-09/MY%20CHEMICAL%20ROMANCE%20ANNOUNCE%20%20THE%20BLACK%20PARADE%202026.pdf) identifies the first three as the tour's closing North American run. Live Nation separately lists [30 October with The Used](https://www.livenation.com/event/vvG1iZbS55yKJr/my-chemical-romance-with-special-guest-the-used) and [31 October with Thrice](https://www.livenation.com/event/vvG1iZbS55BdJV/my-chemical-romance-with-special-guest-thrice).

sections.title: What the different billing lets you decide
sections.content:
If seeing The Used is part of the reason for going, shortlist 30 October. If it is Thrice, shortlist 31 October. If the advertised Black Parade tour is the attraction, start with 21, 23 and 24 October and read the specific event details before paying.

That is a useful distinction, but it has a boundary: **an event title is not a setlist**. The later listings do not establish which MCR songs will be played, and the Halloween date alone does not establish a special performance. Nothing in this comparison promises a particular song or an identical show across nights. Guest billing can change; recheck the promoter's event page when booking.

There is a practical difference even if the guest does not matter to you. A 7pm start leaves an hour less for getting from work or a flight to the venue than an 8pm start. Check the event's arrival instructions separately. Do not treat either scheduled start as the time MCR will take the stage.

sections.title: Compare tickets within your shortlist
sections.content:
Once the night is fixed, compare the same quantity and the same kind of seat. A pair together, two separate seats and a single ticket answer different needs, even when their first displayed figures look similar. Check section, row, seat arrangement and any view restriction on the provider's listing. The [ticket-listing guide](/guides/how-to-read-a-ticket-listing) explains those fields.

The [MCR ticket-price page](/artists/my-chemical-romance/ticket-prices) organises tracked dates and any eligible provider-listed snapshots by city. Use each date's own comparison links. Any displayed figure belongs to that event and provider at the capture time shown; it is not a final checkout total or evidence that a particular seat remains purchasable.

If several nights suit you, open each separately and compare actual listings that meet your needs, including the final order total. There is no supported claim here that a Wednesday, a Halloween show or a later-added date costs less. The [comparison guide](/guides/how-to-compare-concert-ticket-prices) covers how to check totals without mixing unlike tickets.

sections.title: Keep the date attached to the purchase
sections.content:
Before paying, match the full date on the listing and order summary to the night you selected. Then check the ticket delivery deadline against your travel plans. A confirmation email and a transferred ticket are different things; the [delivery and transfer guide](/guides/ticket-delivery-and-transfer-timing) explains what to confirm with a resale seller.

The useful order is simple: billing, date, seats, total, delivery. Comparing figures first can leave you with a ticket for a concert you did not mean to choose.

sources.label: Live Nation — October 30 listing and other Hollywood Bowl nights
Live Nation — October 31 listing with Thrice
Warner Records — The Black Parade 2026 tour announcement

posts.title: Trans-Siberian Orchestra 2026: matinee or evening tickets?
posts.seoTitle: TSO 2026: matinee or evening? | TourTicketCompare
posts.description: Choosing Trans-Siberian Orchestra tickets for 2026? Check afternoon and evening sessions, family logistics and the exact start time before comparing.
posts.summary: Several stops on Trans-Siberian Orchestra's 2026 winter tour have two performances on the same day. Choose the session your group can attend, then compare tickets for that exact performance.
posts.author: TourTicketCompare

sections.content:
Choose a Trans-Siberian Orchestra matinee if an earlier start fits your group and journey home; choose the evening if the afternoon clashes with work or travel. **Neither session is established as the less expensive option by the evidence here.** For the 2026 winter tour, several cities have two performances on the same date, so the start time is part of identifying the ticket you need.

Start with the [Trans-Siberian Orchestra date board](/artists/trans-siberian-orchestra), then check the full date and time on the provider's listing. Matching the city and day is not enough when the venue hosts both sessions.

sections.title: Confirmed examples of two-show days
sections.content:
The following schedules were checked against official artist or venue pages on 11 October 2026. All times are local to the venue. This is a selection of confirmed examples, not the complete tour schedule.

| Date in 2026 | City and venue | Afternoon | Evening |
|---|---|---|---|
| Saturday 21 November | Denver — Ball Arena | 3pm | 7.30pm |
| Saturday 5 December | Columbus — Nationwide Arena | 3pm | 7.30pm |
| Sunday 20 December | Philadelphia — Xfinity Mobile Arena | 3pm | 7.30pm |

TSO's [Denver page](https://www.trans-siberian.com/pages/market/denver--co?event=Denver_CO) and [Philadelphia page](https://www.trans-siberian.com/pages/market/philadelphia--pa?event=Philadelphia_PA) list both sessions. [Nationwide Arena's Columbus listing](https://www.nationwidearena.com/events/detail/trans-siberian-orchestra-6) does the same.

TTC currently tracks the afternoon performance in each of these three examples. An evening session missing from the date board does not mean the performance does not exist. Use the official schedule to confirm the session you want; the site's checked comparison links apply only to the performance named on their card.

sections.title: An afternoon ticket is still a ticket to the advertised production
sections.content:
The official pages describe the 2026 tour as a new staging of **The Ghosts of Christmas Eve**, followed by a second set. They do not label the afternoon performances as shortened children's shows. Equally, that description does not promise identical running times or song selections across sessions.

For a family booking, an earlier start may make the journey home easier to plan. It does not make the production quieter: the event descriptions mention lasers, pyrotechnics and other effects. Check the venue's child admission, hearing protection and accessibility guidance before choosing seats. Do not assume a child enters free or can share an adult's seat.

For an evening booking, work backwards from the scheduled start to the time you need to arrive. A 7.30pm listing is not a confirmed finishing time. If the last train or bus determines whether the evening works, ask the venue about expected timings before committing.

sections.title: Compare one performance at a time
sections.content:
The easy mistake is opening two listings for the same date and assuming they describe the same event. Check **city, venue, date and start time** before comparing section, row and ticket quantity. A 3pm ticket should not be treated as admission to the 7.30pm performance unless the actual ticket terms explicitly say so.

For sessions TTC tracks, the [TSO ticket-price page](/artists/trans-siberian-orchestra/ticket-prices) brings together the date-specific comparison links and any eligible listed-price snapshots. A displayed figure is one provider's snapshot for that performance, with its capture time. It does not describe the evening session, a family bundle or the final order total.

A group needs a listing that meets its seating requirements, rather than a headline figure for a single seat. Confirm whether the seats are together and compare the total for everyone attending. The [listing guide](/guides/how-to-read-a-ticket-listing) and [ticket-price comparison guide](/guides/how-to-compare-concert-ticket-prices) cover those checks.

sections.title: Delivery matters when someone else is taking the group
sections.content:
If you are buying as a gift or for relatives, establish who will hold the tickets on show day. Nationwide Arena says its mobile tickets are not valid as paper printouts or screenshots; its event page explains the arrangements for guests without a smartphone. Those are Columbus instructions, not a rule to assume for every tour stop.

Check the chosen venue's own entry method and the seller's delivery deadline. The [delivery and transfer guide](/guides/ticket-delivery-and-transfer-timing) helps distinguish an order confirmation from a ticket ready for entry. Choosing the right session is only useful if the person going can receive and use the tickets.

posts.title: Bruno Mars at Falcon Stadium: September 2026 entry guidance
posts.seoTitle: Bruno Mars: Falcon Stadium entry 2026 | TourTicketCompare
posts.description: Entry guidance for Bruno Mars’ 26–27 September 2026 Falcon Stadium concerts. These dates have passed; find current dates on the artist page.
posts.summary: The 26–27 September 2026 Falcon Stadium dates have passed. This article records the access guidance for those concerts, not the arrangements for a future event. For upcoming shows, start with the current Bruno Mars date list and check the instructions for that exact show.
posts.author: TourTicketCompare

sections.content:
**These concert dates have passed.** The guidance below relates to the 26 and 27 September 2026 Falcon Stadium dates listed on Bruno Mars’ official tour page. It should not be used as the access plan for a future concert. [Check current Bruno Mars dates and ticket links](/artists/bruno-mars) for upcoming shows, then read the venue's instructions for the date you choose.

For future concerts, the [Bruno Mars ticket price guide](/artists/bruno-mars/ticket-prices) groups the currently listed dates by city. A price appears only where a fresh, provider-attributed snapshot can be shown. Match the date and venue, then confirm the seat details and final total with the ticket site; the historical access guidance below does not apply to those other venues.

Falcon Stadium is inside the United States Air Force Academy, so the September 2026 guidance covered access to the installation as well as the stadium. A concert ticket identifies the show and admission category; access instructions need to be checked separately for everyone travelling together.

sections.title: Start with the instructions for your concert
sections.content:
The Academy’s general visitor page describes sponsored passes, identification checks and screening. It also recognises special-event access arrangements. Those general rules are useful background, but they are not enough to tell every concertgoer which pass, gate or registration process applies on their date.

Read the Academy’s concert information and the messages attached to your booking before you travel. If they do not explain your circumstances, ask the Academy’s Pass and Registration Office to confirm. Do not use a registration link for a different event, or assume that an ordinary visitor pass covers your concert.

Check for each person in your group whether advance registration is required, which original identification they need, and whether their citizenship or documents require an in-person visit. The Academy publishes separate instructions for non-U.S. citizens. Its published office hours have not always agreed between one section of the site and another, so confirm any appointment you need directly with the office rather than planning around a quoted opening time.

sections.title: Match the arrival plan to your ticket
sections.content:
The Academy’s floor-seating guidance directs floor ticketholders through the South Gate and into the stadium at Gate 3, with wristband collection inside. It also gives separate instructions for rideshare arrivals. Read that guidance if you hold a floor ticket; do not assume the same route applies to every seating category.

Before leaving, keep the concert date, ticket category, parking or rideshare instructions and entry guidance together. If friends bought different ticket types, compare the instructions before agreeing a meeting point. Leave time for the checks described by the Academy and consult the latest event guidance for arrival times.

The concert has its own published bag policy too. Check its size limits and exceptions before packing, particularly if you need to carry medical items or supplies for an infant. A bag accepted at another venue may not meet this event’s rules.

sections.title: What the ticket comparison can tell you
sections.content:
The [Bruno Mars page](/artists/bruno-mars) lists the verified dates with provider links checked for each event. Any price shown is one ticket site’s listed price, with when it was checked. It doesn’t include a promise about installation access, a particular seat or your final checkout total.

Open the button for your chosen date and check the provider’s event, seating and delivery details. Keep that ticket check separate from the Academy’s access instructions: completing one does not establish that the other is complete. The [delivery and transfer guide](/guides/ticket-delivery-and-transfer-timing) explains what to check when tickets will reach your account later.
